title: Moment of Inertia of a Cylinder
short_intro: The moment of inertia of a rigid cylinder depends on its mass, radius, length, and the specific geometric axis of rotation chosen. It governs the rotational dynamics of cylindrical bodies about longitudinal or transverse axes.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Calculation of moment of inertia of a solid and hollow cylinder about its geometric longitudinal axis using elementary integration and standard formulae.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Application of perpendicular and parallel axis theorems to find the moment of inertia of a cylinder about an axis passing through its centre of mass perpendicular to its length, and about its edge.

prerequisites: Definition of moment of inertia (I = sum m_i r_i^2)
Integration techniques for continuous mass distributions

concept_notes.heading: Hollow Cylinder (Thin Cylindrical Shell)
bullets: All the mass M is concentrated at a constant perpendicular distance R from the longitudinal axis.
The moment of inertia about its own geometric axis is given by I = MR^2.
It is independent of the length L of the cylinder because every mass element is at distance R from the axis.

concept_notes.heading: Solid Cylinder
bullets: Mass is distributed continuously from radius r = 0 to r = R inside the volume.
The moment of inertia about its longitudinal geometric axis is I = (1/2)MR^2.
It depends only on mass M and radius R, remaining independent of length L for rotation about the central longitudinal axis.

concept_notes.heading: Transverse Axis through Centre of Mass
bullets: For a solid cylinder of mass M, radius R, and length L rotating about a transverse axis through its centre of mass perpendicular to its length, I = (1/4)MR^2 + (1/12)ML^2.
Derived by integrating elemental circular discs of thickness dx along the length.
Accounts for both radial distribution of mass and longitudinal extension.

concept_notes.heading: Hollow Cylinder about Transverse Axis through CM
bullets: For a thin hollow cylindrical shell of radius R and length L rotating about its transverse axis through the centre of mass, I = (1/2)MR^2 + (1/12)ML^2.
Combines the shell formula about its own axis with the rod formula for longitudinal distribution.
Directly utilized in advanced rotational dynamics problems.

derivations.title: Moment of Inertia of a Solid Cylinder about its Longitudinal Axis
derivations.conditions: Uniform solid cylinder of mass M, radius R, and length L rotating about its central geometric axis.
steps: Consider the solid cylinder as a collection of coaxial cylindrical shells of radius r, thickness dr, and length L.
The volume of a shell is dV = 2 pi r dr L, and its mass is dm = (M / (pi R^2 L)) * (2 pi r dr L) = (2M / R^2) r dr.
The moment of inertia of this elemental shell is dI = r^2 dm = (2M / R^2) r^3 dr.
Integrate dI from r = 0 to r = R to get the total moment of inertia.

derivations.title: Moment of Inertia of a Solid Cylinder about a Transverse Axis through its Centre of Mass
derivations.conditions: Solid cylinder of mass M, radius R, and length L, axis perpendicular to the length passing through the mid-point.
steps: Consider an elemental circular disc of thickness dx at a distance x from the centre along the length.
The mass of the disc is dm = (M / L) dx, and its moment of inertia about its own diameter is dI_d = (1/4) dm R^2.
Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of this disc about the transverse axis through the centre of the cylinder is dI = dI_d + (dm) x^2 = (1/4) (M/L) R^2 dx + (M/L) x^2 dx.
Integrate x from -L/2 to L/2: I = integral_{-L/2}^{L/2} [ (1/4)(M/L)R^2 + (M/L)x^2 ] dx.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Torsional Pendulum Experiment
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A solid cylinder suspended by a vertical wire oscillating torsionally, with a graph of T^2 versus I.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The square of the time period T^2 is directly proportional to the moment of inertia I of the suspended system, yielding a straight line whose slope determines the torsional rigidity of the wire.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Tested conceptually for experimental determination of moment of inertia and verification of time period formula T = 2 pi sqrt(I / C).

graphs_and_experiments.title: Incline Rolling Experiment
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Acceleration a versus (1 / (1 + k^2/R^2)) for a cylinder rolling down an inclined plane.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Shows how geometric mass distribution parameter (radius of gyration k) controls translational acceleration during rolling without slipping.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Relates linear acceleration, time of descent, and moment of inertia.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Moment of Inertia vs Radius Square Graph
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A linear graph plotting I on the y-axis and R^2 on the x-axis for a set of solid cylinders of same mass and length.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: A straight line passing through the origin with a slope equal to half the mass (M/2).
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Interpretation of proportionality constants in experimental physics viva voce and objective matching questions.

solved_numericals.question: Find the moment of inertia of a solid cylinder of mass 4 kg and radius 0.2 m about its central longitudinal axis.
solution_steps: Identify the formula for the moment of inertia of a solid cylinder about its longitudinal axis: I = (1/2)MR^2.
Substitute the given values: M = 4 kg, R = 0.2 m.

solved_numericals.question: A solid cylinder has a mass of 2 kg, radius 0.1 m, and length 0.5 m. Calculate its moment of inertia about a transverse axis passing through its centre of mass perpendicular to its length.
solution_steps: Use the formula for transverse axis through CM: I = (1/4)MR^2 + (1/12)ML^2.
Substitute M = 2 kg, R = 0.1 m, L = 0.5 m.

solved_numericals.question: Determine the moment of inertia of a hollow cylinder of mass 5 kg and radius 0.3 m about a tangent parallel to its axis of symmetry.
solution_steps: Use the formula for a hollow cylinder about a tangential longitudinal axis: I = 2MR^2.
Alternatively, apply the parallel axis theorem: I = I_cm + Md^2 = MR^2 + M(R)^2 = 2MR^2.
Substitute M = 5 kg and R = 0.3 m.

assumptions_and_limitations: The cylinder is assumed to be rigid, meaning no internal deformation occurs during rotation.
Mass density is assumed to be strictly uniform throughout the volume unless specified otherwise as a function of radius.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The moment of inertia of a solid cylinder depends on its length when rotating about its longitudinal axis.
common_misconceptions.correct: It is independent of length L for rotation about the longitudinal axis.
common_misconceptions.why: All mass elements lie at radial distances independent of the longitudinal coordinate z.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The formula I = MR^2 applies to solid cylinders.
common_misconceptions.correct: I = MR^2 applies strictly to thin hollow cylindrical shells or rings.
common_misconceptions.why: Solid cylinders have mass distributed radially from 0 to R, yielding the factor 1/2 instead of 1.

quick_revision: Solid cylinder longitudinal axis: I = 0.5 MR^2; Hollow cylinder longitudinal axis: I = MR^2.
Solid Cylinder (Longitudinal Axis): I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2
Hollow Cylinder / Thin Shell (Longitudinal Axis): I = M R^2
